before: nth-child() counts element siblings, starting at one. p:nth-child(2) matches a paragraph only when it is the second element child. nth-of-type() counts only siblings with the same element type.

In p:nth-of-type(2), the p before the colon selects paragraphs and the 2 inside parentheses requests the second paragraph among its siblings. Text nodes do not count as element positions. odd and even select alternating positions. This is a CSS selector function, not a JavaScript call; it returns matching elements conceptually, not a value your program receives.

after: A pseudo-class adds a condition to a selector. `:nth-child(2)` means “is the second element inside its parent.” In `p:nth-child(2)`, that second element must also be a paragraph. Counting starts at 1 and ignores plain text between elements.
`:nth-of-type(2)` counts only elements with the same tag name. `p:nth-of-type(2)` chooses the second paragraph among its siblings. A heading before the paragraphs does not count as a paragraph.
Adding another heading does not change which paragraph is second. Adding a paragraph before it does. You can also use `odd` or `even` instead of a number to choose alternating positions.
